passages.title: Glory fills the completed tabernacle
passages.excerpt: Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the LORD’s glory filled the tabernacle.
passages.observation: After the commanded work is raised and arranged, cloud and glory fill the tabernacle and govern Israel’s movement.

passages.title: Glory appears when priestly service begins
passages.excerpt: Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting, and came out, and blessed the people; and the LORD’s glory appeared to all the people.
passages.observation: Moses and Aaron enter and leave the Tent of Meeting before glory and fire appear to the people.

passages.title: Unauthorized fire reaches the sanctuary boundary
passages.excerpt: Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron, and said to them, “Draw near, carry your brothers from before the sanctuary out of the camp.”
passages.observation: Nadab and Abihu die before the LORD; bodies are carried outside, mourning is bounded, and priestly distinctions are restated.

passages.title: Access to the Holy Place is bounded
passages.excerpt: and the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron your brother not to come at just any time into the Most Holy Place within the veil, before the mercy seat which is on the ark;…
passages.observation: Aaron is warned not to enter at any time, and the chapter orders cleansing, blood, confession, and atonement.

passages.title: Sabbath and sanctuary reverence stand together
passages.excerpt: “‘You shall keep my Sabbaths, and reverence my sanctuary; I am the LORD.
passages.observation: A compact command places Sabbath keeping beside reverence for the LORD’s sanctuary.

passages.title: Sanctuaries can be made desolate
passages.excerpt: I will lay your cities waste, and will bring your sanctuaries to desolation. I will not take delight in the sweet fragrance of your offerings.
passages.observation: Covenant warnings name ruined cities, desolate sanctuaries, interrupted offerings, and exile.

passages.title: Leaders bring gifts to the anointed tabernacle
passages.excerpt: On the day that Moses had finished setting up the tabernacle, and had anointed it and sanctified it with all its furniture, and the altar with all its vessels, and had…
passages.observation: The completed tabernacle is set up, anointed, and supplied through a long ordered sequence of tribal offerings.

passages.title: Cloud and fire govern the tabernacle journey
passages.excerpt: On the day that the tabernacle was raised up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, even the Tent of the Testimony. At evening it was over the tabernacle, as it were the a…
passages.observation: Cloud covers the tabernacle by day, fire appears by night, and Israel camps or travels at the LORD’s command.

passages.title: Sanctuary responsibility is assigned
passages.excerpt: The LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your fathers’ house with you shall bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons with you shall bear the ini…
passages.observation: Aaron, his sons, and the Levites receive differentiated responsibility for sanctuary, priesthood, gifts, and approach.

passages.title: Moses and Aaron fall at the Tent of Meeting
passages.excerpt: Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and fell on their faces. The LORD’s glory appeared to them.
passages.observation: The leaders leave the assembly, fall facedown at the tent entrance, and encounter glory before the water command.

passages.title: Leadership succession comes to the Tent
passages.excerpt: The LORD said to Moses, “Behold, your days approach that you must die. Call Joshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Meeting, that I may commission him.” Moses an…
passages.observation: Moses and Joshua present themselves at the Tent of Meeting as Moses’ death and Israel’s future are addressed.

passages.title: The tabernacle is set up at Shiloh
passages.excerpt: The whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled themselves together at Shiloh, and set up the Tent of Meeting there. The land was subdued before them.
passages.observation: The gathered congregation establishes the Tent of Meeting at Shiloh while land remains to be apportioned.

passages.title: An altar dispute appeals to the LORD’s tabernacle
passages.excerpt: However, if the land of your possession is unclean, then pass over to the land of the possession of the LORD, in which the LORD’s tabernacle dwells, and take possessio…
passages.observation: Eastern tribes and western representatives debate purity, rebellion, witness, and the one established altar.

passages.title: An engraved image persists while God’s house is at Shiloh
passages.excerpt: So they set up for themselves Micah’s engraved image which he made, and it remained all the time that God’s house was in Shiloh.
passages.observation: Dan’s captured shrine and priestly line are located in time against the continuing house of God at Shiloh.

passages.title: Hannah prays beside the Shiloh temple
passages.excerpt: So Hannah rose up after they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat by the doorpost of the LORD’s temple.
passages.observation: Hannah rises in grief, speaks silently before the LORD, and is observed by Eli at the sanctuary doorpost.

passages.title: Shiloh service is corrupted and judged
passages.excerpt: Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did to all Israel, and how that they slept with the women who served at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
passages.observation: Reports about Eli’s sons at the Tent of Meeting stand beside warning, delayed restraint, and an announced end to Eli’s house.

passages.title: Samuel hears a voice in the LORD’s temple
passages.excerpt: and God’s lamp hadn’t yet gone out, and Samuel had laid down in the LORD’s temple where God’s ark was,
passages.observation: The lamp, ark, repeated call, Eli’s recognition, and Samuel’s response structure the night scene.

passages.title: The ark enters the tent David pitched
passages.excerpt: They brought in the LORD’s ark, and set it in its place in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings…
passages.observation: David brings the ark into the prepared tent, offers sacrifices, blesses the people, and distributes food.

passages.title: David’s proposed house meets a divine question
passages.excerpt: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘The LORD says, “Should you build me a house for me to dwell in?
passages.observation: David’s settled house and the ark’s tent prompt a proposal, while the oracle reverses who will build a house.

passages.title: A cry is heard from God’s temple
passages.excerpt: In my distress, I called on the LORD. Yes, I called to my God. He heard my voice out of his temple. My cry came into his ears.
passages.observation: David’s song moves from distress and prayer to divine hearing, earth-shaking arrival, and rescue.

passages.title: David’s altar marks a halted plague
passages.excerpt: David built an altar to the LORD there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. So the LORD was entreated for the land, and the plague was removed from Israel.
passages.observation: At Araunah’s threshing floor David buys the site, builds an altar, offers sacrifices, and the plague is stopped.

passages.title: Solomon announces a house for the LORD’s name
passages.excerpt: Behold, I intend to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, as the LORD spoke to David my father, saying, ‘Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your plac…
passages.observation: Rest from enemies and the promise to David frame Solomon’s decision to build.

passages.title: The house takes architectural form
passages.excerpt: The porch in front of the temple of the house had a length of twenty cubits, which was along the width of the house. Ten cubits was its width in front of the house.
passages.observation: Measurements, chambers, materials, inner sanctuary, carved work, and doors accumulate through the building account.

passages.title: The bronze sea holds two thousand baths
passages.excerpt: It was a hand width thick. Its brim was worked like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It held two thousand baths.
passages.observation: The furnishings account measures the molten sea, its rim, supports, and stated capacity within the completed house works.

passages.title: Ark, cloud, prayer, and dedication converge
passages.excerpt: It came to pass, when the priests had come out of the holy place, that the cloud filled the LORD’s house,
passages.observation: The ark enters, cloud fills the house, Solomon addresses God’s name and heavenly dwelling, and the assembly dedicates the house.

passages.title: God names the dedicated house and its warning
passages.excerpt: The LORD said to him, “I have heard your prayer and your supplication that you have made before me. I have made this house holy, which you have built, to put my name t…
passages.observation: After Solomon’s prayer, God says his name and eyes will be at the house while attaching continued dwelling to covenant conduct.

passages.title: A chest gathers money for temple repair
passages.excerpt: But Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into the LORD’s house; and the priests wh…
passages.observation: Jehoiada places a chest near the altar; counted money moves to supervisors and workers repairing damaged parts of the house.

passages.title: Ahaz moves the bronze altar
passages.excerpt: The bronze altar, which was before the LORD, he brought from the front of the house, from between his altar and the LORD’s house, and put it on the north side of his a…
passages.observation: A copied altar is installed, the bronze altar is displaced, and priestly service is reordered by royal command.

passages.title: Hezekiah strips gold from the temple doors
passages.excerpt: At that time, Hezekiah cut off the gold from the doors of the LORD’s temple, and from the pillars which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave it to the king of…
passages.observation: Under Assyrian pressure, tribute reaches the gold Hezekiah had placed on the LORD’s temple.

passages.title: Josiah removes vessels made for other gods
passages.excerpt: The king commanded Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out of the LORD’s temple all the vessels th…
passages.observation: Covenant reading and reform move through the temple, its vessels, personnel, altars, and surrounding worship sites.

passages.title: Temple treasures are carried away
passages.excerpt: He carried out from there all the treasures of the LORD’s house and the treasures of the king’s house, and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold which Solomon king of…
passages.observation: The Babylonian king removes treasures and cuts apart objects Solomon had made as Jerusalem is subdued.

passages.title: The Babylonian officer burns the temple
passages.excerpt: He burned the LORD’s house, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem. He burned every great house with fire.
passages.observation: The dated arrival of Nebuzaradan is followed by burning the LORD’s house, royal buildings, and Jerusalem’s great houses.

passages.title: Tabernacle song continues until Solomon builds
passages.excerpt: They ministered with song before the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting until Solomon had built the LORD’s house in Jerusalem. They performed the duties of their office…
passages.observation: Singers serve before the Tent of Meeting until the house in Jerusalem is established.

passages.title: Chronicles retells the house oracle
passages.excerpt: “Go and tell David my servant, ‘The LORD says, “You shall not build me a house to dwell in;
passages.observation: David’s wish to build, the history of tent dwelling, and the promised descendant’s house are restated.

passages.title: Fire answers at the future temple site
passages.excerpt: David built an altar to the LORD there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on the LORD; and he answered him from the sky by fire on the altar…
passages.observation: David builds at Ornan’s threshing floor, fire answers from heaven, and fear of the drawn sword fixes his attention on the site.

passages.title: David identifies the future temple site
passages.excerpt: Then David said, “This is the house of the LORD God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
passages.observation: After altar and fire, David names the location as the house of the LORD God and prepares for Solomon’s work.

passages.title: Solomon receives the sanctuary pattern
passages.excerpt: Take heed now, for the LORD has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong, and do it.”
passages.observation: David charges Solomon, gives plans for spaces and service, and attributes the pattern to divine instruction.

passages.title: Preparation becomes a public offering
passages.excerpt: Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the bronze for the things of bronze…
passages.observation: David’s prepared materials, personal treasure, leaders’ gifts, and public blessing gather around the house.

passages.title: Workers are counted for the house
passages.excerpt: Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand men who were stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.
passages.observation: Solomon assigns burden bearers, stone cutters, and overseers before describing the house he intends to build.

passages.title: Chronicles describes the Most Holy Place
passages.excerpt: He made the most holy place. Its length, according to the width of the house, was twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits; and he overlaid it with fine gold, amount…
passages.observation: Dimensions, gold, cherubim, pillars, and named features give the house a concentrated architectural account.

passages.title: The bronze sea holds three thousand baths
passages.excerpt: It was a handbreadth thick. Its brim was made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It received and held three thousand baths.
passages.observation: Chronicles describes the sea’s thickness, supports, use, and stated capacity among the temple furnishings.

passages.title: The ark and Tent vessels enter the house
passages.excerpt: They brought up the ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the Tent. The Levitical priests brought these up.
passages.observation: Priests and Levites bring the ark, Tent of Meeting, and holy vessels as singers and glory fill the house.

passages.title: Solomon prays toward a house God cannot contain
passages.excerpt: But the LORD said to David my father, ‘Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart;
passages.observation: The dedication holds the built house, God’s name, heaven, prayer, forgiveness, exile, and return together.

passages.title: Fire and glory answer the dedication prayer
passages.excerpt: Now when Solomon had finished praying, fire came down from heaven and consumed the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and the LORD’s glory filled the house.
passages.observation: Fire consumes the offerings, glory fills the house, the priests cannot enter, and the assembly bows and praises.

passages.title: Jehoshaphat prays before the sanctuary
passages.excerpt: They lived in it, and have built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying,
passages.observation: Threat drives Judah to the house, where covenant history and the sanctuary’s name frame a communal appeal.

passages.title: The house is abandoned after Jehoiada
passages.excerpt: They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and served the Asherah poles and the idols, so wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem for this their guiltin…
passages.observation: Leaders leave the LORD’s house for other worship, prophets warn, and violence reaches the temple court.

passages.title: Uzziah crosses the sanctuary boundary
passages.excerpt: But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up, so that he did corruptly and he trespassed against the LORD his God, for he went into the LORD’s temple to burn incens…
passages.observation: Royal strength turns to pride when Uzziah enters to burn incense and priests oppose him.

passages.title: Hezekiah opens and cleanses the house
passages.excerpt: and said to them, “Listen to me, you Levites! Now sanctify yourselves, and sanctify the house of the LORD, the God of your fathers, and carry the filthiness out of the…
passages.observation: Doors, vessels, priests, Levites, removal of uncleanness, sacrifice, music, and worship mark renewed service.

passages.title: Repair uncovers the book of the law
passages.excerpt: Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he had purged the land and the house, he sent Shaphan the son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the…
passages.observation: Josiah’s temple repair leads to a found book, royal hearing, inquiry, covenant renewal, and reform.

passages.title: The house and city fall together
passages.excerpt: Therefore he brought on them the king of the Chaldeans, who killed their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and had no compassion on young man o…
passages.observation: The closing judgment gathers slain people, desecrated sanctuary, burned house, broken wall, exile, and Cyrus’s decree.

passages.title: Cyrus authorizes rebuilding in Jerusalem
passages.excerpt: Whoever there is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of the LORD, the God of I…
passages.observation: A royal proclamation credits the God of heaven and releases people and goods for the house.

passages.title: Worship resumes before foundations are laid
passages.excerpt: From the first day of the seventh month, they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD; but the foundation of the LORD’s temple was not yet laid.
passages.observation: Altar, offerings, feast, resources, foundation, song, shouting, and weeping mark the return.

passages.title: Opposition interrupts rebuilding
passages.excerpt: Now when the adversaries of Judah and Benjamin heard that the children of the captivity were building a temple to the LORD, the God of Israel,
passages.observation: Neighbors offer participation, are refused, discourage the builders, and use imperial correspondence.

passages.title: The rebuilt house is dedicated
passages.excerpt: The children of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this house of God with joy.
passages.observation: Decree, supplied costs, completion, dedication, priestly ordering, Passover, and joy close the rebuilding sequence.

passages.title: The restored house is named as a peg of grace
passages.excerpt: Now for a little moment grace has been shown from the LORD our God, to leave us a remnant to escape, and to give us a stake in his holy place, that our God may lighten…
passages.observation: Ezra’s confession situates remnant, sanctuary, bondage, and renewed life inside remembered failure.

passages.title: A proposed refuge inside the temple is refused
passages.excerpt: I went to the house of Shemaiah the son of Delaiah the son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at his home; and he said, “Let us meet together in God’s house, within the tem…
passages.observation: Shemaiah urges Nehemiah to hide in the temple, but Nehemiah recognizes the proposal as hired intimidation.

passages.title: The community binds itself to temple provision
passages.excerpt: Also we made ordinances for ourselves, to charge ourselves yearly with the third part of a shekel for the service of the house of our God:
passages.observation: Tax, bread, offerings, wood, first fruits, tithes, and Levite service are gathered under a pledge not to forsake the house.

passages.title: A temple room is reassigned and cleansed
passages.excerpt: Now before this, Eliashib the priest, who was appointed over the rooms of the house of our God, being allied to Tobiah,
passages.observation: Eliashib provides Tobiah a room; Nehemiah expels the goods, cleanses the rooms, and restores provisions.

passages.title: Earthly temple and heavenly throne share one line
passages.excerpt: The LORD is in his holy temple. The LORD is on his throne in heaven. His eyes observe. His eyes examine the children of men.
passages.observation: The psalm places the LORD in his holy temple and on his heavenly throne before describing divine sight and testing.

passages.title: Who may ascend and stand in the holy place?
passages.excerpt: Who may ascend to the LORD’s hill? Who may stand in his holy place?
passages.observation: The psalm moves from creator and world to ascent, clean hands, blessing, gates, and the entering King of glory.

passages.title: One request centers on the LORD’s house
passages.excerpt: One thing I have asked of the LORD, that I will seek after: that I may dwell in the LORD’s house all the days of my life, to see the LORD’s beauty, and to inquire in h…
passages.observation: Dwelling, beauty, inquiry, shelter, song, and seeking gather inside a prayer under threat.

passages.title: The sanctuary changes the psalmist’s sight
passages.excerpt: until I entered God’s sanctuary, and considered their latter end.
passages.observation: Envy and confusion turn when the speaker enters God’s sanctuary and perceives the end of the prosperous.

passages.title: The sanctuary’s destruction becomes lament
passages.excerpt: Lift up your feet to the perpetual ruins, all the evil that the enemy has done in the sanctuary.
passages.observation: Enemies, fire, signs, silence, covenant appeal, and remembered divine power shape the communal prayer.

passages.title: A threshold is preferred to other dwellings
passages.excerpt: For a day in your courts is better than a thousand. I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God, than to dwell in the tents of wickedness.
passages.observation: Longing, pilgrimage, altars, strength, prayer, and one day in God’s courts accumulate in the song.

passages.title: Prayer seeks Jerusalem’s good for God’s house
passages.excerpt: For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good.
passages.observation: Pilgrimage joy, tribes, thrones, peace, kinship, and the LORD’s house gather in a city-directed prayer.

passages.title: Night servants bless from the sanctuary
passages.excerpt: Lift up your hands in the sanctuary. Praise the LORD!
passages.observation: A brief song addresses those who stand in the LORD’s house and lifts hands toward the sanctuary.

passages.title: Steps and speech are guarded at God’s house
passages.excerpt: Guard your steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t know that they do evil.
passages.observation: Drawing near to listen is set against foolish sacrifice, rash words, delayed vows, and unguarded speech.

passages.title: Isaiah sees the Lord in the temple
passages.excerpt: In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.
passages.observation: Throne, robe, seraphim, holiness, shaking, smoke, confession, coal, and commission unfold in the vision.

passages.title: Sanctuary princes are profaned
passages.excerpt: Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; and I will make Jacob a curse, and Israel an insult.”
passages.observation: A dispute about witness, failure, and redemption ends by naming sanctuary officials, Jacob’s curse, and Israel’s reproach.

passages.title: A house of prayer for all peoples
passages.excerpt: I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my hou…
passages.observation: Foreigners, covenant keeping, joyful worship, offerings, gathering, and the house’s public name are joined.

passages.title: Nations’ glory adorns the sanctuary
passages.excerpt: “The glory of Lebanon shall come to you, the cypress tree, the pine, and the box tree together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary; and I will make the place of my…
passages.observation: Restoration language gathers peoples, resources, light, gates, holiness, and the place of God’s feet.

passages.title: A voice of recompense sounds from the temple
passages.excerpt: A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of the LORD that repays his enemies what they deserve.
passages.observation: The closing oracle contrasts humanly chosen worship with divine arrival, birth, comfort, judgment, and new creation.

passages.title: The temple sermon rejects a repeated slogan
passages.excerpt: Don’t trust in lying words, saying, ‘The LORD’s temple, the LORD’s temple, the LORD’s temple, are these.’
passages.observation: Jeremiah confronts trust in “the LORD’s temple” while naming conduct, Shiloh, judgment, and possible dwelling.

passages.title: The sanctuary is called a glorious throne
passages.excerpt: A glorious throne, set on high from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
passages.observation: A short confession places Israel’s hope, living water, forsaking, and a glorious sanctuary together.

passages.title: The temple sermon places Jeremiah on trial
passages.excerpt: “The LORD says: ‘Stand in the court of the LORD’s house, and speak to all the cities of Judah which come to worship in the LORD’s house, all the words that I command y…
passages.observation: A command to speak in the temple court leads to accusation, defense, remembered precedent, and Ahikam’s protection.

passages.title: Fugitives announce vengeance for the temple
passages.excerpt: Listen to those who flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance of his temple.
passages.observation: Escape from Babylon becomes proclamation in Zion about the LORD’s temple and Babylon’s fall.

passages.title: Jeremiah dates the burning of the temple
passages.excerpt: He burned the LORD’s house, and the king’s house; and all the houses of Jerusalem, even every great house, he burned with fire.
passages.observation: A second destruction account dates Nebuzaradan’s arrival and narrates the burning, wall demolition, exile, and dismantled bronze.

passages.title: Tabernacle, assembly, altar, and sanctuary collapse
passages.excerpt: He has violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were a garden. He has destroyed his place of assembly. The LORD has caused solemn assembly and Sabbath to be forgo…
passages.observation: The lament names dismantled sacred space alongside forgotten festivals, rejected rulers, and public grief.

passages.title: Ezekiel is shown detestable acts in the sanctuary
passages.excerpt: He said to me, “Son of man, do you see what they do? Even the great abominations that the house of Israel commit here, that I should go far off from my sanctuary? But…
passages.observation: The vision moves through entrances and chambers where escalating practices are displayed.

passages.title: Glory leaves the temple threshold
passages.excerpt: The LORD’s glory went out from over the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubim.
passages.observation: The glory moves from the threshold to the cherubim and east gate as the visionary departure advances.

passages.title: God promises to be a sanctuary in dispersion
passages.excerpt: “Therefore say, ‘The Lord GOD says: “Whereas I have removed them far off among the nations, and whereas I have scattered them among the countries, yet I will be to the…
passages.observation: Judgment on Jerusalem’s leaders is held beside gathering, changed hearts, and a sanctuary among scattered people.

passages.title: An enduring sanctuary follows reunion
passages.excerpt: Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them. It will be an everlasting covenant with them. I will place them, multiply them, and will set my sanctuary among the…
passages.observation: Joined people, one king, cleansing, covenant of peace, dwelling, and sanctuary form the promise’s sequence.

passages.title: A measured temple vision begins
passages.excerpt: In the visions of God he brought me into the land of Israel, and set me down on a very high mountain, on which was something like the frame of a city to the south.
passages.observation: Ezekiel is brought to Israel in a vision and shown a citylike structure before a guide begins measuring gates and courts.

passages.title: The visionary temple is measured
passages.excerpt: He measured its length, twenty cubits, and the width, twenty cubits, before the nave. He said to me, “This is the most holy place.”
passages.observation: Rooms, walls, doors, carved forms, and the Most Holy Place are measured in an extended architectural vision.

passages.title: Glory returns and altar service begins
passages.excerpt: You shall also take the bull of the sin offering, and it shall be burned in the appointed place of the house, outside of the sanctuary.
passages.observation: The returning glory, east gate, altar measurements, purification, and offerings order the renewed house.

passages.title: Returned glory fills the house
passages.excerpt: Then he brought me by the way of the north gate before the house; and I looked, and behold, the LORD’s glory filled the LORD’s house; so I fell on my face.
passages.observation: At the north gate Ezekiel sees the LORD’s glory filling the temple, falls down, and receives new boundary instructions.

passages.title: Water flows from the temple threshold
passages.excerpt: He brought me back to the door of the temple; and behold, waters flowed out from under the threshold of the temple eastward, for the front of the temple faced toward t…
passages.observation: A measured river deepens, heals waters, sustains trees, and leaves some marshes unchanged.

passages.title: The restored city receives a final name
passages.excerpt: “It shall be eighteen thousand reeds in circumference; and the name of the city from that day shall be, ‘The LORD is there.’
passages.observation: After tribal allotments and gates are measured, the city’s circumference is stated and its name declares the LORD’s presence.

passages.title: Temple vessels enter a foreign treasury
passages.excerpt: The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with some of the vessels of the house of God; and he carried them into the land of Shinar to the house of his god.…
passages.observation: Jerusalem’s defeat is narrated through captured king and vessels placed in the house of another god.

passages.title: Temple vessels become feast vessels
passages.excerpt: Belshazzar, while he tasted the wine, commanded that the golden and silver vessels which Nebuchadnezzar his father had taken out of the temple which was in Jerusalem b…
passages.observation: Belshazzar orders Jerusalem vessels brought to the banquet; rulers drink from them and praise material gods before the hand appears.

passages.title: The vision reaches the sanctuary and offering
passages.excerpt: Yes, it magnified itself, even to the prince of the army; and it took away from him the continual burnt offering, and the place of his sanctuary was cast down.
passages.observation: A horn magnifies itself, removes the continual offering, casts down sanctuary, and prompts a duration question.

passages.title: Daniel asks God to shine on the desolate sanctuary
